title: Absence of Rate Limiting on Authentication and VIP Registration Endpoints
description: The Express application in FloresByDolly has no rate limiting middleware configured. Public endpoints POST /api/auth/login and POST /api/registro can be queried without restriction, exposing the application to password brute-force attacks and automated PII scraping.
root_cause: Missing rate-limiting middleware (such as express-rate-limit) on sensitive Express routes.
intended_behavior: The application should enforce per-IP and per-account rate limits to mitigate brute force and denial of service.

trace.description: Express server initializes without rate limiting middleware.
Exposes login endpoint without request throttle.
Performs password comparison on every request without backoff or lockout.

evidence.description: Dependencies list lacks express-rate-limit or equivalent.

conditions.description: Attacker sends high-frequency HTTP requests over the network.

execution.attacker_perspective: An attacker uses an automated tool against /api/auth/login.
payloads: for i in $(seq 1 100); do curl -s -X POST http://localhost:3010/api/auth/login -d '{"username":"admin","password":"wrong"}' -H 'Content-Type: application/json'; done
instructions: Send rapid concurrent POST requests to /api/auth/login.
Observe that no 429 Too Many Requests response is returned.
execution.observed_result: Server processes all requests without throttling.

remediation.strategy: Install express-rate-limit and apply strict limits to auth and registration endpoints.

likelihood.reason: Automated brute force against unthrottled login endpoints is trivial to execute.

impact.reason: Exposes administrative accounts to credential compromise and allows resource exhaustion.

confidence.reason: Confirmed by package.json and server.js route definitions.

title: Missing HTTP Security Headers and Information Disclosure in FloresByDolly
description: The Express backend in FloresByDolly does not utilize helmet or custom security header middleware. It fails to send X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, X-Frame-Options, or Strict-Transport-Security headers, and leaks the technology stack via the X-Powered-By: Express header.
root_cause: Absence of helmet or defensive HTTP header middleware in server.js.
intended_behavior: The application should send defensive HTTP headers and suppress technological fingerprinting headers.

trace.description: Initializes Express application without security headers middleware.
Serves static files without nosniff protection.
Emits responses with default X-Powered-By: Express and without defensive security headers.

evidence.description: app.use(cors(...)); // helmet is not imported or mounted

conditions.description: Victim visits a malicious third-party website embedding the target in an iframe.

execution.attacker_perspective: An attacker inspects HTTP response headers using curl or browser devtools.
execution.observed_result: Response contains X-Powered-By: Express and lacks X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, and CSP.

remediation.strategy: Install and mount helmet middleware in server.js and disable x-powered-by header.

likelihood.reason: Headers are missing on every HTTP response served by the backend.

impact.reason: Permits clickjacking of embedded views, MIME confusion attacks on static uploads, and framework fingerprinting.

title: Missing Authentication on Internal and Host-Bound MongoDB Instance
description: The FloresByDolly MongoDB service runs mongo:latest exposed to 127.0.0.1:27017 on the host and unauthenticated on the Docker bridge network. No administrative username or password is configured in docker-compose.yml or backend/config/db.js.
root_cause: Omitting MONGO_INITDB_ROOT_USERNAME, MONGO_INITDB_ROOT_PASSWORD, and the --auth flag in the MongoDB container configuration.
intended_behavior: MongoDB should run with authentication enforced (--auth) and require a secure username and password for all database operations.

trace.description: Exposes unauthenticated MongoDB listener on host 127.0.0.1:27017.
Connects to database without user credentials: mongoose.connect(process.env.MONGODB_URI).

conditions.description: Attacker has access to the local server host or a container sharing the Docker bridge network.

execution.attacker_perspective: A local service, adjacent container (such as compromised whatsapp-bot), or user on the server connects to port 27017.
instructions: Connect to MongoDB using mongosh without credentials.
execution.observed_result: Full read and write access to all collections with zero authentication.

remediation.strategy: Enable authentication in docker-compose.yml, generate strong credentials, update MONGODB_URI to include credentials, and remove host port mapping if not needed externally.

code_changes.fixed_code:
mongodb:
    image: mongo:latest
    container_name: flores-mongodb
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      MONGO_INITDB_ROOT_USERNAME: ${MONGO_ROOT_USER}
      MONGO_INITDB_ROOT_PASSWORD: ${MONGO_ROOT_PASSWORD}
    command: mongod --auth
    volumes:
      - mongodb_data:/data/db

likelihood.reason: MongoDB port is exposed and connection requires no authentication handshake.

impact.reason: Allows complete database theft, deletion, or modification by any local process or container.

confidence.reason: Confirmed by inspecting docker-compose.yml, backend/.env, and backend/config/db.js.

title: Unauthenticated PII Data Harvesting and User Record Overwriting in POST /api/registro
description: The public raffle registration endpoint POST /api/registro checks if a phone number already exists in the RegistroVip collection. If found, it overwrites the user name with the attacker-supplied name and returns the complete Mongoose document in data: existente, disclosing the full name, phone number, and all previously referred contacts with their private phone numbers.
root_cause: Unconditionally updating the existing user record and returning the complete entity in the public JSON response without authentication or authorization.
intended_behavior: The public registration endpoint should reject duplicate submissions with a generic conflict response or return an opaque acknowledgment without exposing existing user details or modifying existing records without verified identity (OTP).

trace.description: Exposes unauthenticated public POST endpoint for raffle registration.
Queries database for existing record: const existente = await RegistroVip.findOne({ celular: celular.trim() }).
Overwrites existing record name: existente.nombre = nombre.trim(); existente.activo = true; await existente.save();
Serializes and returns complete user document: res.json({ success: true, message: '...', data: existente, updated: true }).

evidence.description: const existente = await RegistroVip.findOne({ celular: celular.trim() });

conditions.description: Endpoint is public and unauthenticated by design.
Endpoint is accessible from the internet via Cloudflare Tunnel.

execution.attacker_perspective: An unauthenticated attacker sends a registration request containing a target 10-digit phone number with dummy referral data.
payloads:
POST /api/registro HTTP/1.1
Host: www.floresbydolly.com
Content-Type: application/json

{"nombre": "Pwned User", "celular": "3001234567", "referidos": [{"nombre": "Dummy", "celular": "3009999999"}]}
instructions: Issue a POST request to /api/registro with an existing customer mobile number.
Observe HTTP 200 response returning data: existente with victim full name, phone number, and all previously recorded referrals.
execution.observed_result: Response leaks full name, mobile number, and array of referred friends/family with their personal phone numbers. The database record is also updated with the attacker-controlled name.

remediation.strategy: Do not return existing user entities in public responses. Return an opaque HTTP 409 Conflict message when a number is already registered, and require OTP verification for any profile modification.

likelihood.reason: The endpoint is completely unauthenticated and can be enumerated programmatically by iterating standard mobile phone prefixes.

impact.reason: Causes bulk exfiltration of personally identifiable information (PII) including third-party referral contacts, and allows unauthorized tampering with customer records.

confidence.reason: Confirmed by source code inspection in registro.controller.js and verified independently.
